en.title: Street Fighter Box Office Projections Hint at a Tough Opening Round
en.summary: Early box office estimates for the new Street Fighter movie suggest a challenging debut, potentially falling short of its production budget. Fans are watching closely to see if the film can overcome a crowded release schedule and mixed early buzz.
en.body:
The roar of the crowd might be a little quieter at the box office this week, as early projections for the new **Street Fighter** movie indicate a less-than-stellar opening. The film, hitting theaters with previews starting Thursday, is expected to take in under $70 million worldwide. Breaking that down, domestic forecasts hover in the high $30 millions on over 3,500 screens, with international markets adding a similar amount. For a film with an $82 million production cost, this means recouping its expenses in the first weekend looks unlikely.

This financial outlook places **Street Fighter** in a precarious position, especially when compared to its Capcom cousin, **Resident Evil**. The latter film, released earlier this year, enjoyed a robust $60 million domestic opening and has since grossed an impressive $324 million worldwide, becoming a significant commercial hit. In contrast, **Mortal Kombat 2** saw a considerably weaker launch. While **Street Fighter** boasts an international cast and aims for global appeal, it faces the tough reality of Hollywood's often unforgiving box office metrics.

## A Rocky Start for Ryu?

Despite the franchise's global recognition and a cast featuring recognizable faces from various industries, the initial box office tracking suggests a cautious reception. Some reports place the domestic opening even lower, around $20-25 million. This is a stark contrast to the $60 million debut of **Resident Evil**, which exceeded its own initial projections. The film's release date, October 16, 2026, places it in a competitive autumn slot. While it will be the biggest action film for a few weeks, the upcoming November 1 re-release of **V for Vendetta** for its 20th anniversary could draw some attention away.

The movie also won't see a release in the crucial Chinese market, a significant omission for a global blockbuster. International expectations lean towards strong performance in Mexico, Brazil, the UK, Australia, and other Asian markets, but the overall global total needs to significantly outperform initial predictions to be considered a success. With early reviews described as mixed, the film's ultimate box office fate may hinge on strong word-of-mouth driving audiences to theaters in the weeks following its debut.

## What Fans Can Expect

For dedicated **Street Fighter** fans, the mixed early buzz and conservative box office projections present a familiar dilemma: will this adaptation finally break the cycle of divisive video game movies, or will it become another cautionary tale? The game's rich history, spanning decades and multiple iconic characters, provides a deep well of material, but translating that magic to the screen has historically proven challenging. The global appeal of the IP is undeniable, and the international cast is a positive step, but the ultimate success will depend on whether the film resonates with both hardcore fans and casual moviegoers alike.

## Looking Ahead

All eyes will be on the opening weekend figures to see if **Street Fighter** can defy its early projections. The film's performance in its first few weeks will be critical in determining its long-term box office viability and whether it can become a profitable venture for its producers. Further updates on box office performance will be closely monitored.

content_raw: Street Fighter is officially spin-kicking its way into theaters this week, starting with previews on Thursday and leading into the crucial opening weekend. It's the second movie based on a Capcom IP to make its way to the silver screen this year--following Zach Cregger's Resident Evil film in September--but so far, early estimates for the martial arts extravaganza aren't looking too healthy. According to Deadline's box-office-predictions , Street Fighter is expected to take in under $70 million worldwide. Of that figure, it's estimated to open with a US box-office take in the high 30 millions on 3,500 screens, and a take in the mid-30 millions internationally. Typically, movies need to make at least double their production budget back to be considered successful, and with Street Fighter costing $82 million to produce, it doesn't look like it'll recoup its expenses in its first weekend. There's still a chance it could be a small hit if word of mouth drives audiences to theaters, and in terms of competition, Street Fighter has a few weeks to dominate cinemas as it'll be the biggest action film on the block--at least until the November 1 re-release of V for Vendetta, which is celebrating its 20th anniversary. The movie won't open in the potentially lucrative market of China, but internationally, the lion's share of sales is expected to come from Mexico, Brazil, the UK, Australia, and Asian markets. How does that opening stack up against other recent video game movie adaptations? Resident Evil got off to a solid start with a $60 million domestic opening last month, and so far, the film has grossed $324 million worldwide, making it a surprise commercial hit and Cregger's biggest film yet . Meanwhile, Mortal Kombat 2 did much worse when it launched in May, making only $38 million on its opening US weekend and finishing with a worldwide box office total of $129.5 million. As for the other Street Fighter movies, they've had mixed results. According to Box Office Mojo , the first Street Fighter movie starring Jean-Claude Van Damme made $99.4 million during its run, which is pretty great for a 1994 flick, but 2009's Street Fighter: The Legend of Chun-Li was a huge flop. It had an opening weekend of $4.7 million in the US, and it made $12.7 million worldwide.
